summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with fevers, cough, and shortness of breath found to be due to a new left lower lobe pneumonia. He had brown sputum and worsening dyspnea, with a history of COPD and multiple myeloma. He was treated with IV Cefepime, Vancomycin, and Levofloxacin, with improvement in symptoms and sputum clearance. His COPD was managed with continued Symbicort and Spiriva, and he remained off supplemental oxygen. His Warfarin dose was adjusted due to a high INR of 3.7 interacting with Levofloxacin; he was instructed to hold Warfarin on discharge day, take 5 mg the next day, and follow up with the anticoagulation clinic. He was discharged home on oral Levofloxacin for a full 14-day course, with stable mental status and baseline breathing. Follow-up was arranged with his primary and specialty providers.
